thread:
elaine_cs: FYI — enterprise customer reported rerank returns all 0.0 scores for every candidate. They sent a payload that mixes 'items' and 'candidates' and we can't reproduce yet.
jun_eng: Can you paste the exact payload they used? most issues are shape-related.
elaine_cs: Here is the minimal repro they provided:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{ "query": "best espresso machines", "items": [{"candidates": [{"id":"c1","text":"Gaggia Classic"},{"id":"c2","text":"Breville Barista"}]}, {"documents": [{"id":"d1","text":"Nespresso Vertuo"}]}] }'```
elaine_cs: They said endpoint returns 200 but all scores are 0.0 and ranking is unchanged.
bryce_prod: Oof — nested collection inside items seems likely. Our API expects either top-level "candidates" OR top-level "documents" (with optional "passages" inside docs), not an array-of-objects with embedded arrays.
jun_eng: Agreed. The parser flattens top-level candidates/docs only. If both exist or are nested under another array key, we treat them as empty and fall back to default scoring (zeros).
elaine_cs: Customer is blocked, asked for a patch or workaround.
jun_eng: Immediate workaround: send candidates at top-level like:```json
{"query":"best espresso machines","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"Gaggia Classic"},{"id":"c2","text":"Breville Barista"}]}```
jun_eng: Also try moving any free-form object arrays into top-level fields.
bryce_prod: Can we return a clear 422 with a message like "unexpected nested candidates in 'items' — please put candidates at top-level"? Right now it's 200 which is confusing.
jun_eng: Yeah, the current behavior is legacy. I'll open an infra ticket to change response code and add a schema validation layer. For quick fix I can add a short help text in response body if we detect nested arrays.
elaine_cs: Customer wants repro steps for us to confirm before we change docs. They can run the following to see working vs broken:```bash
# broken (nested)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query":"x","items":[{"candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"a"}]}]}' | jq '.'
# fixed (top-level candidates)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query":"x","candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"a"}]}' | jq '.'
```
support-bot: INCIDENT-6723 created by jun_eng — schema-validation middleware + better error for nested candidate/document arrays. ETA: 2 sprints. :white_check_mark:
elaine_cs: I'll send the workaround to customer and offer to validate a sanitized payload if they paste it here.
jun_eng: One more note — "query" name collisions inside each item can also shadow top-level query. If the payload has a per-item query we ignore it unless clients use the explicit "item_query" flag. Might be worth documenting.
bryce_prod: Good call. Make a short doc PR: examples for candidates, documents-with-passages, and an anti-pattern section showing nested containers that break serialization.
elaine_cs: I'll follow up with customer and mark thread resolved once they confirm the top-level payload works. Thanks all. :pray:
